hints: For each position, measure a match with the whole string's prefix.
The Z-function starts its match at that position; the prefix function ends its match there.
Both arrays can reuse information from earlier positions to run in linear time.
analogy: The Z-function asks how much a suffix resembles the start; the prefix function asks how much of the start appears at the end of a prefix.
example: For ababa, the Z values are 0,0,3,0,1 and the prefix-function values are 0,0,1,2,3.
algorithm: Compute Z using the rightmost interval matching a prefix: initialize from its mirror when inside the interval, then extend. Compute the prefix function by following earlier border lengths on mismatch and extending on a match. Print both arrays in the required order.
correctness: The Z interval supplies only already-proved matching characters and extension finds the exact remaining length. The prefix-function fallback enumerates all possible shorter borders, so its first match is the longest border.
complexity: For length n, O(n) time and O(n) space.
